clue.text: Restriction on entry that may be lifted

definitions.text: Restriction on entry that may be lifted

parts.words: Restriction on entry that may be lifted
parts.note: a castle gate's iron grille barred entry and was hauled up to let people through

explanation.definitionFit: The grille dropped across a castle gateway is raised to admit visitors, so it is a liftable barrier to entry.

clue.text: This musical work is nothing to Manx cat

parts.note: O is the round shape of zero, nothing

indicators.note: a Manx cat is born without a tail, so the word for cat loses its final letter

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: A piece of music means nothing to a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: A Manx cat (from the Isle of Man) has no tail, so 'Manx' docks the last letter of PUSS, leaving PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin word for a work, used for a numbered musical composition.

clue.text: Growing economy?

parts.note: reads as an expanding national economy, but means careful saving and also a seaside plant that grows

explanation.definitionFit: Thrift means frugal economy, and it is also the sea pink, a plant that grows on cliffs.

clue.text: We hear you possibly enlist in domestic service, perhaps

indicators.note: We hear means the word that follows is heard, so a single letter sounding like it is used

parts.note: the word you is said exactly like the letter U

indicators.note: possibly says the letters that follow could be put in another order

explanation.surface: Rumour has it you may join up to work as a household servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' sounds you as U; 'possibly' rearranges ENLIST to TENSIL. A kitchen tool is 'in domestic service' in the sense of being used at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool such as a spoon or whisk is used in the home, serving in the household.

clue.text: Number taking turn at party game

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a U-turn, so U is a turn
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Several guests take their turn at a game during a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party game' looks like one phrase, but the party is DO and only 'game' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game played with dice and coloured counters.

clue.text: Staying terribly dark and gloomy

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lingering somewhere that is dreadfully dark and depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges STAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian comes from the River Styx of the underworld, hence pitch dark and gloomy.

clue.text: Sea seems to be quite calm, fortunately

definitions.text: Sea seems to be quite calm
definitions.meaning: the sea shows merely a gentle rolling wave and nothing worse
luckily, it is a good thing

explanation.surface: Sailors are relieved that the sea looks gentle today.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way, the phrase says the sea has only a gentle rolling motion; as an idiom it means luckily.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something worked out for the best means it was fortunate; a swell is a gentle sea.

clue.text: Digs for convalescents

parts.note: digs are lodgings, and patients recovering in bed are those who sit up in it

explanation.definitionFit: One-room flats are called digs, and patients on the mend sit up in bed.

clue.text: Scored a point-could be winning

parts.note: to score is to cut a line into a surface
E is east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A competitor reckons that scoring one point might just win the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' and 'winning' suggest a sporting result, but scored means cut, and 'winning' is the adjective for charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile is a charming, appealing one, the same sense as sweet and endearing.

clue.text: Six hours' time to pay

definitions.meaning: six hours is one fourth of a twenty-four-hour day
the four traditional dates in the year when rent and dues fell due in England

explanation.surface: Someone is given six hours to settle a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: A QUARTER DAY is one of four days in the British calendar (such as Lady Day) on which rents were paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, a fourth of a day is six hours; as a fixed term, the phrase names a traditional rent-paying date.

clue.text: Soldiers hold deserter without charge

indicators.note: the soldiers hold the deserter, so that word goes inside

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is one who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: Troops detain a runaway without bringing any charge against him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without charge' looks legal, as in releasing a suspect, but it means free of cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given free costs nothing, so it comes without any charge.

clue.text: Not ripe perhaps, but needed for one's diet

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Fruit that is unripe may still be something your diet requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges NOTRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is a nutrient the body requires, an essential part of any healthy eating plan.

clue.text: Labour exchange?

parts.note: looks like a jobcentre, but means a place where letters and parcels are exchanged

explanation.walkthrough: A labour exchange was the old British name for a jobcentre.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail branch is an exchange point for letters and parcels, and its counter staff perform labour.

clue.text: Path of the swallow?

parts.note: looks like the migration route of a bird, but a swallow of food travels down the gullet

explanation.definitionFit: The gullet carries swallowed food from throat to stomach, so it is the route a swallow takes.

clue.text: Ian went back to ad for Nymph

indicators.note: went back means the name is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Ian returned to an advertisement featuring a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went back' turns IAN into NAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek mythology, living in rivers and springs.

clue.text: Unyielding and difficult games on the tennis court

parts.note: hard means difficult
a set in tennis is a group of games

explanation.surface: A tough tennis match drags on through stubborn, difficult games.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firmly solidified or fixed will not give way, so it is rigid and unyielding.

clue.text: It beats a man with skill

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
art is skill

explanation.surface: Something defeats a skilled man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It beats' looks like 'it defeats', but it is the organ that pumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ that pumps blood keeps beating throughout life.

clue.text: Left port with cargo

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship departed harbour carrying a full cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left port' reads as a ship departing, but left is just L and the port is Aden.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship carrying a cargo is loaded down, a synonym of weighed with goods.

clue.text: Band giving some of Sousa's hits

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A marching band plays a selection of John Philip Sousa's famous marches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks musical, fitting Sousa the march composer, but it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a strip of fabric worn round the waist or over a shoulder, a kind of band.

clue.text: Apportion food, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the word for food is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: meat is food

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to share out the provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to dole out or distribute shares, so it means apportion.

clue.text: Will possibly includes one TV producer

indicators.note: the first word includes the second, which goes inside it

parts.note: Will Shakespeare is known as the Bard; possibly marks him as an example
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A last testament may leave something to a television maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a legal testament, but it is Shakespeare, the Bard. John Logie Baird was the Scottish pioneer of television.
explanation.definitionFit: John Logie Baird demonstrated the first working television, so he produced the TV itself.

clue.text: Gives the call-sign

parts.note: sounds like radio identification, but means signals to someone to come over

explanation.definitionFit: Summoning someone with a wave of the hand is giving a sign that calls them.

clue.text: Shuffling cards it is necessary to be vigorous

indicators.note: shuffling cards mixes them, so these letters are mixed too

explanation.surface: When shuffling a pack you must be energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffling' rearranges CARDSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are forceful and extreme, so vigorous in their effect.

clue.text: Objected to work, took up modelling

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a model posed for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone protested at having to work after becoming a model.
explanation.definitionFit: If you opposed a plan you argued against it, so you objected to it.

clue.text: A likely backer for the training of climbers

definitions.text: A likely backer for the training of climbers

parts.words: A likely backer for the training of climbers
parts.note: reads like a sponsor of mountaineering courses, but the climbers are plants trained up a garden framework

explanation.definitionFit: A lattice fixed to a wall supports climbing plants as gardeners train them upward.

clue.text: Shrub that's evergreen but not hardy!

definitions.text: Shrub that's evergreen but not hardy!

parts.words: Shrub that's evergreen but not hardy
parts.note: an evergreen bush, and also the partner of Oliver Hardy in the famous comedy duo

explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel and Oliver Hardy were a famous comedy double act; the shrub is the bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree is an evergreen shrub, and Stan was the comedy partner who was not Oliver.

clue.text: Open sound of French composer

indicators.note: sound of tells us a word for open is spoken to give a name heard the same way

parts.note: frank means open and candid

explanation.surface: An honest appraisal of how a French composer's music sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: César Franck was a Belgian-born composer who worked in France.
explanation.definitionFit: César Franck, composer of a famous violin sonata, spent his career in Paris as a French composer.

clue.text: Unhappy university sportsman

definitions.meaning: an Oxford or Cambridge athlete who has represented the university

explanation.surface: A college athlete feels miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge, a sportsman who represents the university earns a Blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is feeling sad, and an Oxbridge athlete awarded colours gets this title.

clue.text: Shuffle a set of Greek letters

indicators.note: shuffle means the letters that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: An instruction to mix up a group of Greek characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' rearranges ASET.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet; the plural gives several such letters.

clue.text: Get rid of old boy who is well-read

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
literate means well-read

explanation.surface: Disposing of a former pupil who happens to be bookish.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out completely is to destroy or erase it, getting rid of it.

clue.text: At night a place for a really good bash?

definitions.text: At night a place for a really good bash?

parts.words: At night a place for a really good bash
parts.note: a nightspot for a party, while a bash is also a heavy blow from a stick

explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub hosts parties after dark, and a cudgel is used to strike a heavy blow.

clue.text: Dumbstruck at getting only a walk-on role?

definitions.meaning: too astonished to say a word
an extra who walks on stage has no lines to deliver

explanation.surface: An actor is stunned to be cast only as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lost for words is being dumbstruck; a walk-on part has no lines at all.
